# Register reference {#registers}

This appendix lists the registers of the LiteX-M2SDR gateware, bank by bank. It is generated
from the register definitions of the gateware: the tool runs `litex_m2sdr.py` without
`--build` for the configurations of the table below, which elaborates the SoC without
running Vivado.

One build cannot hold every bank, because PCIe, Ethernet and SATA cannot be enabled
together and the Ethernet PHYs have different registers. The three configurations are
chosen to elaborate every bank once, not as builds to use. White Rabbit builds add the
registers of the White Rabbit core, which this appendix does not list: they need the
external `litex_wr_nic` package.

Offsets are in bytes from the base of the bank. The banks named in `BaseSoC.csr_map`
(`litex_m2sdr.py`) keep the same base address in every build ([The SoC](#soc)); LiteX
places the others. The addresses are in the `csr.csv` and `csr.h` of a build.

| Configuration | Target and options |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `m2_pcie` | `litex_m2sdr.py` `--variant=m2` `--with-pcie` `--with-pcie-ptm` `--with-rfic-oversampling` `--with-gpio` `--with-pcie-probe` |
| `baseboard_eth_sata` | `litex_m2sdr.py` `--variant=baseboard` `--with-eth` `--with-eth-ptp` `--with-eth-ptp-rfic-clock` `--with-eth-vrt` `--with-sata` |
| `baseboard_eth_5g` | `litex_m2sdr.py` `--variant=baseboard` `--with-eth` `--eth-phy=5000baser` |

Access is `rw` for a register written by software (`CSRStorage`, or a `CSRStatus` that
software also writes, such as event pending bits cleared by writing 1), `ro` for a status
(`CSRStatus`) and `wo` for a write-only strobe (`CSR`). The reset value of a `CSRStorage`
register ends its description. A register wider than 32 bits takes several
32-bit words of the bus, most significant word first. 
The utilities and the library use these names through the generated `csr.h`, and the
scripts through `csr.csv`, so they never need the offsets.

## Capability {#reg-capability}

Defined by `Capability` (`litex_m2sdr/gateware/capability.py`).

Read-only description of the build: software reads it first to know which host links and
options the bitstream holds ([The SoC](#soc)).

Bank `capability`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `api_version` | `0x0000` | 32 | ro | API Version of the gateware (e.g., 0x0100 for v1.0). |
| `features` | `0x0004` | 10 | ro | Hardware feature presence bitfield. |
| `pcie_config` | `0x0008` | 5 | ro | PCIe configuration. Valid only if features.pcie is set. |
| `eth_config` | `0x000c` | 4 | ro | Ethernet configuration. Valid only if features.eth is set. |
| `sata_config` | `0x0010` | 4 | ro | SATA configuration. Valid only if features.sata is set. |
| `board_info` | `0x0014` | 5 | ro | Board-level configuration. |

Fields of `features`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `pcie` | 0 | PCIe is present. |
| `eth` | 1 | Ethernet is present. |
| `sata` | 2 | SATA is present. |
| `gpio` | 3 | GPIO is present. |
| `wr` | 4 | White Rabbit is present. |
| `jtagbone` | 5 | JTAGBone is present. |
| `eth_ptp` | 6 | Ethernet PTP time discipline is present. |
| `eth_ptp_rfic_` `clock` | 7 | Ethernet PTP can discipline the RFIC reference clock path. |
| `timed_tx` | 8 | Hardware timed-TX gate (and its timestamp-offset CSRs) is present. |
| `rfic_` `oversampling` | 9 | RFIC oversampling datapath (128-bit, 491.52 MHz, 2T2R@122.88) is present. |

Fields of `pcie_config`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `speed` | 1:0 | PCIe speed configuration. |
| `lanes` | 3:2 | PCIe lanes configuration. |
| `ptm` | 4 | PCIe Precision Time Measurement (PTM) enable status. |

Fields of `eth_config`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `speed` | 1:0 | Ethernet speed configuration. |
| `ptp` | 2 | Ethernet PTP time discipline build support. |
| `ptp_rfic_clock` | 3 | PTP-to-RFIC-reference clock discipline build support. |

Fields of `sata_config`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `gen` | 1:0 | SATA generation configuration. |
| `mode` | 3:2 | SATA mode configuration. |

Fields of `board_info`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `variant` | 1:0 | Board variant. |
| `jtagbone` | 2 | JTAGBone enabled. |
| `eth_sfp` | 3 | Ethernet SFP index. |
| `wr_sfp` | 4 | White Rabbit SFP index. |

## SoC controller (LiteX) {#reg-ctrl}

Defined by `SoCController` (`litex/soc/integration/soc.py`).

Registers of the LiteX SoC controller. `scratch` is the register to read and write to
check a host bridge ([Debugging](#debugging)).

Bank `ctrl`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `reset` | `0x0000` | 2 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `scratch` | `0x0004` | 32 | rw | Use this register as a scratch space to verify that software read/write accesses to the Wishbone/CSR bus are working correctly. The initial reset value of 0x12345678 can be used to verify endianness. Reset `0x12345678`. |
| `bus_errors` | `0x0008` | 32 | ro | Total number of Wishbone bus errors (timeouts) since start. |

Fields of `reset`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `soc_rst` | 0 | Write ``1`` to reset the full SoC (pulse reset). |
| `cpu_rst` | 1 | Write ``1`` to reset the CPU(s) of the SoC (hold reset). |

## ICAP (LiteX) {#reg-icap}

Defined by `ICAP` (`litex/soc/cores/icap.py`).

Access to the configuration logic of the FPGA; the utilities use it to reload the FPGA
from the SPI flash after an update ([Building the gateware](#building-gateware)).

Bank `icap`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `addr` | `0x0000` | 5 | rw | ICAP Address. Reset `0x0`. |
| `data` | `0x0004` | 32 | rw | ICAP Write/Read Data. Reset `0x0`. |
| `write` | `0x0008` | 1 | rw | ICAP Control. Write ``1`` to send a write to the ICAP. Reset `0x0`. |
| `done` | `0x000c` | 1 | ro | ICAP Status. Write command done when read as ``1``. |
| `read` | `0x0010` | 1 | rw | ICAP Control. Write ``1`` to issue a read from the ICAP. Reset `0x0`. |

## GPIO {#reg-gpio}

Defined by `GPIO` (`litex_m2sdr/gateware/gpio.py`).

The core is 4 bits wide; only bits 0 and 1 reach a pin, the test points TP1 and TP2
([Hardware](#hardware)).

Bank `gpio`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `control` | `0x0000` | 3 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `_o` | `0x0004` | 4 | rw | GPIO output data when in CSR mode. Reset `0x0`. |
| `oe` | `0x0008` | 4 | rw | Output enable (tristate control) when in CSR mode. Reset `0x0`. |
| `_i` | `0x000c` | 4 | ro | GPIO input data. |

Fields of `control`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `enable` | 0 | Enable/disable GPIO functionality. |
| `source` | 1 | Select GPIO control source. |
| `loopback` | 2 | Enable/disable internal loopback mode. |

## SI5351 clock generator {#reg-si5351}

Defined by `SI5351` (`litex_m2sdr/gateware/si5351.py`).

The bank holds the registers of the LiteI2C master (`i2c_*`), of the PWM that tunes the
oscillator of the SI5351B version (`pwm_*`) and of the SI5351 control
([Time synchronisation](#timing)).

Bank `si5351`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `i2c_phy_speed_` `mode` | `0x0000` | 2 | rw | I2C speed: 0: 100 kHz, 1: 400 kHz, 2: 1 MHz. Reset `0x0`. |
| `i2c_master_` `active` | `0x0004` | 1 | rw | Write 1 to enable the I2C master. Reset `0x0`. |
| `i2c_master_` `settings` | `0x0008` | 17 | rw | I2C transfer settings Reset `0x0`. |
| `i2c_master_addr` | `0x000c` | 7 | rw | I2C address of the next transfer. Reset `0x0`. |
| `i2c_master_rxtx` | `0x0010` | 32 | rw | Write: push the transmit data. Read: pop the received data. |
| `i2c_master_` `status` | `0x0014` | 18 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `pwm_enable` | `0x0018` | 1 | rw | PWM Enable. Write ``1`` to enable PWM. Reset `0x1`. |
| `pwm_width` | `0x001c` | 32 | rw | PWM Width. Defines the *Duty cycle* of the PWM. PWM is active high for *Width* ``sys_clk`` cycles and active low for *Period - Width* ``sys_clk`` cycles. Reset `0x400`. |
| `pwm_period` | `0x0020` | 32 | rw | PWM Period. Defines the *Period* of the PWM in ``sys_clk`` cycles. Reset `0x800`. |
| `control` | `0x0024` | 9 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `status` | `0x0028` | 9 | ro | `0b0`: Gateware Sequencer Ongoing. `0b1`: Gateware Sequencer Done. |

Fields of `i2c_master_settings`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `len_tx` | 2:0 | I2C tx Xfer length (in bytes). Set to a value greater then 4 to anounce more data has to be transmitted. |
| `len_rx` | 10:8 | I2C rx Xfer length (in bytes). Set to a value greater then 4 to anounce more data has to be received. |
| `recover` | 16 | I2C recover bus. If set, the I2C bus will be recovered. |

Fields of `i2c_master_status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `tx_ready` | 0 | TX FIFO is not full. |
| `rx_ready` | 1 | RX FIFO is not empty. |
| `nack` | 8 | Error on transfer. |
| `bus_error` | 9 | I2C bus error on transfer. |
| `tx_unfinished` | 16 | Another tx transfer is expected. |
| `rx_unfinished` | 17 | Another rx transfer is expected. |

Fields of `control`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `version` | 0 | `0b0`: SI5351B Version. `0b1`: SI5351C Version. |
| `clkin_src` | 1 | `0b0`: 10MHz ClkIn from FPGA (clk10). `0b1`: 10MHz ClkIn from uFL. |
| `ss_en` | 2 | `0b0`: SI5351B Spread spectrum disabled. `0b1`: SI5351B Spread spectrum enabled. |
| `seq_reset` | 8 | `0b1`: Gateware Sequencer Reset. |

## Clock measurement {#reg-clk-measurement}

Defined by `MultiClkMeasurement` (`litex_m2sdr/gateware/measurement.py`).

Each clock has a free-running 64-bit counter. Software latches the counters twice and
divides the difference by the elapsed time to get a frequency, as `scripts/test_clks.py`
does ([Debugging](#debugging)).

Bank `clk_measurement`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `clk0_latch` | `0x0000` | 1 | wo | Write: latch the counter of the system clock into `clk0_value`. |
| `clk0_value` | `0x0004` | 64 | ro | Latched count of cycles of the system clock. |
| `clk1_latch` | `0x000c` | 1 | wo | Write: latch the counter of the PCIe clock (0 without PCIe) into `clk1_value`. |
| `clk1_value` | `0x0010` | 64 | ro | Latched count of cycles of the PCIe clock (0 without PCIe). |
| `clk2_latch` | `0x0018` | 1 | wo | Write: latch the counter of the AD9361 reference clock (SI5351 output 0) into `clk2_value`. |
| `clk2_value` | `0x001c` | 64 | ro | Latched count of cycles of the AD9361 reference clock (SI5351 output 0). |
| `clk3_latch` | `0x0024` | 1 | wo | Write: latch the counter of the AD9361 data clock into `clk3_value`. |
| `clk3_value` | `0x0028` | 64 | ro | Latched count of cycles of the AD9361 data clock. |
| `clk4_latch` | `0x0030` | 1 | wo | Write: latch the counter of the board time reference clock (SI5351 output 1) into `clk4_value`. |
| `clk4_value` | `0x0034` | 64 | ro | Latched count of cycles of the board time reference clock (SI5351 output 1). |
| `clk5_latch` | `0x003c` | 1 | wo | Write: latch the counter of the FPGA 10 MHz clock into `clk5_value`. |
| `clk5_value` | `0x0040` | 64 | ro | Latched count of cycles of the FPGA 10 MHz clock. |
| `latch_all` | `0x0048` | 1 | wo | Write: latch the six counters at the same time. |

## Board time {#reg-time-gen}

Defined by `TimeGenerator` (`litex_m2sdr/gateware/time.py`).

The board time is a 64-bit count of nanoseconds ([Streaming](#streaming)). The field
`sync_enable` of `control` has no effect: the SoC does not connect the PPS input to the
board time.

Bank `time_gen`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `control` | `0x0000` | 4 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x1`. |
| `read_time` | `0x0004` | 64 | ro | Read Time (ns) (FPGA Time -\> SW). |
| `write_time` | `0x000c` | 64 | rw | Write Time (ns) (SW Time -\> FPGA). Reset `0x0`. |
| `time_adjustment` | `0x0014` | 64 | rw | Time Adjustment Value (ns) (SW -\> FPGA). Reset `0x0`. |
| `time_inc` | `0x001c` | 32 | rw | Time Increment in ns per tick (Q8.24 format). Reset `0xa000000`. |

Fields of `control`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `enable` | 0 | `0b0`: Time Generator Disabled. `0b1`: Time Generator Enabled. |
| `read` | 1 | Write 1: latch the board time into `read_time` (pulse). |
| `write` | 2 | Write 1: load `write_time` into the board time (pulse). |
| `sync_enable` | 3 | `0b0`: Sync (Re-)Alignment Disabled. `0b1`: Sync (Re-)Alignment Enabled. |

(`pcie_dma1` and the next ones). The PPS input of the start synchroniser is connected
on channel 0 only.

Reset `0x0`. |
| `writer_table_` `loop_status` | `0x0014` | 32 | ro | Loop monitoring for software synchronization. |

Reset `0x0`. |

Clear prbs_pause and wait for prbs_paused to clear before requesting another snapshot. Disabling the checker clears the counter, even while paused. For a bit error ratio, the denominator is the elapsed time times the block rate, linerate/66, times 66 bits per block. |

| `p_gain` | `0x002c` | 16 | rw | Proportional gain applied to the phase error before rate trim limiting. Reset `0x8`. |
| `status` | `0x0030` | 10 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `time_inc` | `0x0034` | 32 | ro | Disciplined TimeGenerator increment (Q8.24 ns/tick). |
| `last_error` | `0x0038` | 64 | ro | Last signed PTP minus board-time error (ns, two's complement). |
| `last_ptp_time` | `0x0040` | 64 | ro | Last sampled PTP time (ns). |
| `last_local_time` | `0x0048` | 64 | ro | Last sampled board time (ns). |
| `coarse_steps` | `0x0050` | 32 | ro | Number of coarse board-time realignments. |
| `phase_steps` | `0x0054` | 32 | ro | Number of bounded phase trims. |
| `rate_updates` | `0x0058` | 32 | ro | Number of rate trim updates. |
| `ptp_lock_losses` | `0x005c` | 32 | ro | Number of PTP lock-loss events observed by the discipline loop. |
| `time_lock_` `misses` | `0x0060` | 32 | ro | Number of out-of-window samples tolerated while time lock was held. |
| `time_lock_miss_` `count` | `0x0064` | 32 | ro | Current consecutive out-of-window sample count while time lock is held. |
| `time_lock_` `losses` | `0x0068` | 32 | ro | Number of deglitched board-time lock-loss events observed by the discipline loop. |

Fields of `control`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `enable` | 0 | `0b0`: Disable PTP ownership of the board time generator. `0b1`: Discipline the board time generator from Ethernet PTP. |
| `holdover` | 1 | `0b0`: Drop back to acquire mode when PTP lock is lost. `0b1`: Keep the last disciplined rate while waiting for PTP lock to return. |

Fields of `status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `enable` | 0 | PTP time discipline enabled. |
| `active` | 1 | PTP discipline currently owns the board time generator. |
| `ptp_locked` | 2 | LiteEth PTP core is locked to a master. |
| `time_locked` | 3 | Board time is within the lock window of PTP time. |
| `holdover` | 4 | PTP lock was lost; keeping the last disciplined rate. |
| `state` | 9:8 | PTP time discipline state. |

## PTP 10 MHz clock discipline {#reg-ptp-clk10-discipline}

Defined by `PTPClock10Discipline` (`litex_m2sdr/gateware/clock_discipline.py`).

Present with `--with-eth-ptp-rfic-clock`.

Bank `ptp_clk10_discipline`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `control` | `0x0000` | 10 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x2`. |
| `update_cycles` | `0x0004` | 32 | rw | MMCMPhaseDiscipline update interval used while the PTP-to-10MHz loop owns clk10. Reset `0x14`. |
| `p_gain` | `0x0008` | 32 | rw | Proportional gain in Q0.32 MMCM fine steps per update per sys-clock tick of phase error. Reset `0x40000`. |
| `i_gain` | `0x000c` | 32 | rw | Integral gain in Q0.32 MMCM fine steps per update per sys-clock tick of phase error. Reset `0x10000`. |
| `rate_limit` | `0x0010` | 32 | rw | Absolute MMCM fine phase-step rate limit in Q0.32 steps per update. Reset `0x7fffffff`. |
| `lock_window_` `ticks` | `0x0014` | 32 | rw | PTP-to-10MHz lock window in sys-clock ticks. Reset `0x1388`. |
| `half_period_` `ticks` | `0x0018` | 32 | rw | Maximum phase-detector search window in sys-clock ticks. Reset `0x2faf080`. |
| `status` | `0x001c` | 8 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `phase_tick_ps` | `0x0020` | 32 | ro | Phase detector tick period in picoseconds. |
| `last_error_` `ticks` | `0x0024` | 32 | ro | Last signed clk10-marker minus PTP-reference phase error in sys-clock ticks. |
| `last_error_ns` | `0x0028` | 64 | ro | Last signed clk10-marker minus PTP-reference phase error in nanoseconds. |
| `last_rate` | `0x0030` | 32 | ro | Last MMCM fine phase-step rate command, signed Q0.32 steps per update. |
| `sample_count` | `0x0034` | 32 | ro | Number of valid PTP-to-10MHz phase samples. |
| `reference_count` | `0x0038` | 32 | ro | Number of PTP reference pulses observed. |
| `clk10_count` | `0x003c` | 32 | ro | Number of clk10 1Hz marker pulses observed. |
| `missing_count` | `0x0040` | 32 | ro | Number of phase-detector windows that expired before the matching marker arrived. |
| `align_count` | `0x0044` | 32 | ro | Number of clk10 marker alignments requested. |
| `lock_loss_count` | `0x0048` | 32 | ro | Number of clk10 marker lock-loss events. |
| `rate_update_` `count` | `0x004c` | 32 | ro | Number of MMCM phase-step rate updates produced by the PTP-to-10MHz loop. |
| `saturation_` `count` | `0x0050` | 32 | ro | Number of rate calculations limited by rate_limit. |

Fields of `control`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `enable` | 0 | `0b0`: PTP-to-10MHz clock discipline disabled. `0b1`: Allow PTP-to-10MHz clock discipline to override the clk10 MMCM phase driver. |
| `holdover` | 1 | `0b0`: Disable MMCM steering when the PTP time reference is not locked. `0b1`: Keep the last MMCM phase-step rate during PTP reference loss. |
| `invert` | 2 | Invert the MMCM phase-step sign used by the PTP-to-10MHz loop. |
| `align` | 8 | Reset the clk10 1Hz phase marker on the next PTP reference pulse. |
| `clear_counters` | 9 | Clear PTP-to-10MHz monitor counters. |

Fields of `status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `enable` | 0 | PTP-to-10MHz clock discipline enabled. |
| `active` | 1 | PTP-to-10MHz loop currently owns the clk10 MMCM phase driver. |
| `reference_` `locked` | 2 | PTP board-time reference is locked. |
| `clock_locked` | 3 | clk10 1Hz marker is within the configured lock window. |
| `holdover` | 4 | PTP reference was lost; keeping the last phase-step rate. |
| `aligned` | 5 | clk10 1Hz marker has been aligned since the loop was enabled. |
| `waiting_after_` `ref` | 6 | Phase detector is waiting for a clk10 marker after the PTP reference pulse. |
| `rate_limited` | 7 | Most recent rate calculation hit the configured rate limit. |

## SATA PHY (LiteSATA) {#reg-sata-phy}

Defined by `LiteSATAPHY` (`litesata/phy/__init__.py`).

The SATA banks are present with `--with-sata`.

Bank `sata_phy`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `enable` | `0x0000` | 1 | rw | 1: SATA PHY enabled, 0: transceiver and initialization held in reset. Reset `0x1`. |
| `status` | `0x0004` | 5 | ro | See the fields below. |

Fields of `status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `ready` | 0 | `0b0`: PHY not initialized. `0b1`: PHY initialized and ready. |
| `tx_ready` | 1 | `0b0`: TX not initialized. `0b1`: TX initialized and ready. |
| `rx_ready` | 2 | `0b0`: RX not initialized. `0b1`: RX initialized and ready. |
| `ctrl_ready` | 3 | `0b0`: Ctrl/OOB not initialized. `0b1`: Ctrl/OOB initialized and ready. |
| `link_up` | 4 | `0b0`: Link down (debounced). `0b1`: Link up. |
